root_cause.text: The zram_bio_discard function returns early without calling bio_endio() when handling partial discard requests that don't align with page boundaries, leaving the bio in an incomplete state and causing callers using submit_bio_wait() to hang indefinitely.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes a bare `return;` statement to `goto end_bio;` at line 2681 in the partial discard handling path. The early return bypassed the bio_endio(bio) call that occurs after the end_bio label, which is necessary to signal completion to the block layer. The commit message explicitly states "we forget to endio on our way out, so blkdiscard sleeps forever in submit_bio_wait()" and the fix ensures all code paths jump to the end_bio label where bio_endio() is called.

bic_trace_step.reason: The zram_bio_discard function contains the vulnerable construct. At lines 23-25, when a discard request has an offset and the remaining size (n) is less than the offset, the function returns early with 'return;' without calling bio_endio(). This leaves the bio in an incomplete state. The bio_endio() call only occurs in __zram_make_request at line 731 after zram_bio_discard returns, but only if the function completes normally. When the early return at line 25 is executed, the function exits without reaching the bio_endio() call in the caller, causing the bio to hang indefinitely if submit_bio_wait() was used. The fix would require calling bio_endio(bio, 0) before the early return statement at line 25.
